label: Reaper station registers of a history's worlds
definition: A ReaperFrame W T assigns to each world u and moment t the code on the output register of the station at t in u (out u t: absent, or a moment naming the station that issued it) and whether the station at t issues its own code in u (issues u t). In ordinary language: a record, world by world, of what a Grim Reaper or Placer station placed at a given moment writes and whether it fires. A world with no station activity has every register empty and no issuing station; the frame says nothing about whether a station is present beyond what it does.
note: Analyst vocabulary for a world-assembly premise in the style of the Koons/Pruss Grim Reaper argument (reconstruction in docs/notes/causal-finitism-367.md); attribution deferred. The registers are extensional: they record what happens in a world, not powers, counterfactual dispositions or intrinsic properties. They are not tied to the history's ExistsAt or IsAt, so register activity has no existential import: the GrimReaperPatchwork controls realize a pair of pieces in a world where nothing exists. The bridge from recombining concrete stations (bearers with powers that exist in a world) to premises stated over these registers is not built; any verdict about the philosophical patchwork principle concerns that principle, not this typed premise. Codes are moments rather than numerals so that a code names a station of the history itself. Whether the registers of any real possible world are faithfully described this way is OPEN.
